message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 140, "amount_cents": 13659}, {"order_id": 144, "amount_cents": 19464}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Start by listing the orders so I can see which customers are in the batch before checking balances.
The orders list shows six orders across three customers. Before paying, I'll check the refund ledger to confirm the refunds W2 reported as applied are actually there.
The refund ledger matches W2's report: order 140 for 13659 and order 144 for 19464. Next I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 31766 matches my check: orders 17469 + 27956 = 45425, minus refund 140 of 13659. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 35795 matches my check: orders 21876 + 33383 = 55259, minus refund 144 of 19464. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance next.
Cobalt's net balance of 20917 matches my check: orders 8761 + 12156 = 20917, with no refunds for cobalt. All three balances now match my own arithmetic, so I'll record the first payout for acme.
Acme's payout of 31766 recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 35795 matches my own check, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's balance of 20917 matches my own check (8761 + 12156, no refunds), so I'll record its payout as the last one in the batch.
All three customers have been paid. Each payout matches the net balance and my own check against the orders and refunds, so the batch is complete.
